title: What is a Docker Image?
definition: A read-only, immutable template that contains a set of instructions for creating a Docker container. It includes the application code, libraries, tools, dependencies, and files needed to run the app.
simpleExplanation: A snapshot of a computer hard drive. Once an Image is created, it cannot be changed (immutable). It is the perfect, frozen blueprint used to stamp out live Containers.
realWorldExample: You download the `postgres:15` Image from the internet. It is a 300MB file. You cannot edit the file. But you can use it to spin up 50 separate, running PostgreSQL databases (Containers).

basic: Can you edit a file permanently inside a Docker Image after it has been built?
intermediate: What is the relationship between an Image and a Container?

answers.question: Edit permanently?
answers.answer: No. Images are strictly read-only and immutable. To change a file, you must build a brand new image.

answers.question: Relationship?
answers.answer: An Image is the class definition (the blueprint). A Container is the instantiated object (the live, running instance).
